title: Confronting Abusive Language Online: A Survey from the Ethical and Human Rights Perspective
findings: The paper, a survey of existing research, highlights that a key challenge in abusive language detection is navigating the fine line between acceptable criticism of religious concepts and unacceptable hate speech targeting religious adherents. It uses the example of anti-Islamic discourse inducing hatred towards Muslims to illustrate this complexity. The paper also acknowledges that religion is a protected characteristic in many legal frameworks designed to combat hate speech.

measurement_description: The paper is a survey that discusses the detection of abusive language and hate speech directed at various groups, including those defined by religion. It specifically notes the challenge of distinguishing between acceptable criticism of a religious concept (e.g., a belief system) and hate speech attacking people associated with that religion (e.g., anti-Islamic discourse inducing hatred towards Muslims).
